data.title: FBM KLCI Ends Lower As Buying Rotates Into Smaller Caps
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia ended the trading session of Sept 18 on a softer note, with the benchmark index retreating as investors rotated into smaller-cap stocks, particularly technology and construction counters.

At 5pm, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 9.18 points, or about 0.55%, to 1,665.56 from Sept 17’s close of 1,674.74.

The index moved between 1,661.79 and 1,677.83 during the session.

Despite the weaker benchmark, buying interest remained firm in the broader market. The FBM 70 surged 1.34% to 17,844.02, while the FBM Shariah gained 0.31% to 12,311.99.

The FBM Emas slipped marginally by 0.02% to 12,411.72, while the F4GBM declined 0.12% to 1,005.75.

Meanwhile, Zetrix AI Bhd was the most actively traded stock, falling 4.5 sen to 20 sen after trading more than one billion shares.

AirAsia Group Bhd gained 2.5 sen to 53 sen, while FSBM Holdings Bhd dropped four sen to 6.5 sen.

JAKS Resources Bhd added 1.5 sen to 15.5 sen, while Top Glove Corporation Bhd slipped two sen to 77.5 sen.

The divergence between the FBM KLCI and the stronger FBM 70 underscored the session’s rotation away from large-cap stocks towards selected mid- and smaller-cap names.

data.title: MPI Leads Bursa Gainers, PetDag Tops Losers As Turnover Jumps
data.description:
Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI) led Bursa Malaysia’s gainers while Petronas Dagangan Bhd (PetDag) topped the decliners, as trading activity surged sharply.

MPI jumped RM2.70 to RM42.80, making it the day’s biggest gainer. Sunway Construction Group Bhd followed with a 76 sen increase to RM7.88, while TIME dotCom Bhd gained 49 sen to RM6.41.

Petronas Gas Bhd added 34 sen to RM17.50, while QL Resources Bhd rose 33 sen to RM4.19.

On the losing end, PetDag fell RM1 to RM20.08, leading the decliners. Nestlé (M) Bhd dropped 94 sen to RM89.58, while Hong Leong Bank Bhd shed 56 sen to RM22.54.

PPB Group Bhd declined 35 sen to RM9.36, while Heineken Malaysia Bhd lost 34 sen to RM14.14.

Market breadth nevertheless remained positive, with 625 gainers outpacing 564 decliners. Another 505 counters were unchanged, 1,172 untraded and 22 suspended.

Trading activity accelerated, with turnover surging to 4.91 billion units worth RM4.87 billion compared to 3.6 billion units valued at RM3.25 billion on Sept 17.

data.title: Yen Sinks To Two-Week Low Despite BOJ Hike As Hawkish Fed Adds Pressure
data.description:
The Japanese yen sank to its weakest level in more than two weeks on Sept 18 despite the Bank of Japan (BOJ) raising interest rates, as investors digested a hawkish shift from the US Federal Reserve (Fed) and questioned whether Japan’s tightening was aggressive enough to support the currency.

Reuters reported that the yen weakened as much as 0.8% to 157.145 per US dollar, its lowest since Sept 3, while falling by a similar margin against the euro to 180.32.

The decline came even as the BOJ lifted its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25%, the highest in 31 years and its first increase in three months. The decision was passed by a 7-2 vote, with two board members favouring no change.

The yen’s latest weakness also followed the Fed’s first rate increase in more than three years.

The Fed raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to a range of 3.75% to 4% this week and signalled that further tightening could follow as policymakers seek to bring inflation back towards the central bank’s 2% target.

Markets are already pricing a 53% probability of another quarter-point Fed hike next month, sharply higher than 27.2% a week earlier, according to CME FedWatch data cited by Reuters.

That prospect could keep the interest-rate gap between the US and Japan wide despite the BOJ’s latest move, maintaining pressure on the yen.

Japan’s core inflation, meanwhile, held near the BOJ’s 2% target in August, keeping attention on Governor Kazuo Ueda for signals on how quickly the central bank could raise rates again.

data.title: FBM KLCI Slips At Midday As Hawkish Fed, Foreign Selling Weigh
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia ended the morning session marginally lower on Sept 18 as cautious sentiment prevailed amid the US Federal Reserve’s hawkish stance, elevated US Treasury yields and persistent foreign selling.

At 12.30pm, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slipped 1.53 points, or 0.09%, to 1,673.21 from its close of 1,674.74 on Sept 17.

The index traded between 1,671.95 and 1,677.83 during the morning session.

The broader market, however, ended the morning session in the positive territory as the FBM 70 gained 0.33% to 17,665.73, while the FBM Emas added 0.05% to 12,421.55. The FBM Shariah advanced 0.19% to 12,297.60.

The broader market also remained positive, with gainers outpacing losers 510 to 460. Another 496 counters were unchanged, while 1,400 were untraded and 22 suspended.

Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd jumped RM2.46 to RM42.56, while Unisem (M) Bhd rose 30 sen to RM4.45. UMS Integration Ltd added 26 sen to RM8.39 and Pentamaster Corporation Bhd gained 23 sen to RM5.45.

Meanwhile, Petronas Dagangan Bhd led the decliners, falling 76 sen to RM20.32, followed by Nestlé (M) Bhd, which lost 48 sen to RM90.04. Hong Leong Bank Bhd shed 32 sen to RM22.78.

Zetrix AI Bhd was the most actively traded counter, slipping one sen to 23.5 sen, followed by FSBM Holdings Bhd at 7.5 sen and AirAsia X parent Capital A-related counters among the more actively traded names.

Overall market turnover stood at 2.01 billion shares valued at RM1.28 billion.

data.title: Stock Today: TNB Slipped 0.9% After Electricity Subsidy Threshold Raised
data.description:
Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) shares fell 0.90% to RM13.20 as of 11.53 am, after the government expanded the electricity subsidy protection threshold from 600kWh to 800kWh per month until the end of 2026.

The stock opened at RM13.32 and moved between an intraday high of RM13.36 and a low of RM13.20. Some 1.39 million shares changed hands.

TNB had closed at RM13.32 in the previous trading session, putting the latest price 12 sen lower.

Under the expanded protection, domestic consumers using up to 800kWh a month will be exempt from the Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), retail charges and the Sales and Service Tax (SST) from September through Dec 31.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the measure was introduced after hotter weather and haze conditions pushed some households above the previous 600kWh threshold, exposing them to AFA charges.

The move follows Tenaga’s clarification earlier this week that AFA is a two-way mechanism reflecting changes in fuel costs and foreign exchange rates, rather than an additional charge imposed by the utility.

Tenaga said consumers had received RM3.1 billion in AFA rebates compared with RM800 million in surcharges since the mechanism was introduced in July 2025.

For September, the AFA rate had been set at a surcharge of 3.67 sen per kWh. The government had also channelled RM435 million through the Electricity Industry Fund to reduce the impact of AFA surcharges on consumers.

data.title: Stock Today: Binastra Holds At RM2.49 After Earnings Surge
data.description:
Binastra Corporation Bhd shares were unchanged at RM2.49 as of 10.54 am, with the construction group holding onto recent gains after reporting a 73% jump in first-half profit to RM92.7 million.

The stock opened at RM2.49 and traded between an intraday high of RM2.52 and a low of RM2.48. Some 865,300 shares changed hands.

Binastra had closed at RM2.49 in the previous trading session, putting the latest price unchanged.

The latest performance follows the group’s results for the six months ended July 31, 2026, which saw revenue nearly double to RM1.3 billion from a year earlier.

Second-quarter revenue rose 65.9% to RM658.4 million, while quarterly PAT surged 90.1% to RM54 million. The construction segment remained the main contributor, supported by data centre projects, conventional construction, solar installation work and contributions from newly acquired LF Lansen Sdn Bhd.

Binastra also secured a RM500 million letter of award during the quarter for a proposed data centre development, taking its outstanding order book to about RM6.7 billion as at end-July.

The group expects the order book to provide earnings visibility over the next four financial years, with continued demand for data centres and industrial facilities in Johor and Selangor supporting its construction pipeline.

Binastra has also declared an interim dividend of four sen per share for FY2027, with entitlement set for Oct 5 and payment on Oct 16.

data.title: Asian Stocks Push Higher With Oil Prices Cooling
data.description:
Asian stocks rose on Friday as easing oil prices and a rebound on Wall Street helped improve sentiment, although investors remained cautious ahead of an expected Bank of Japan (BOJ) rate hike.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan gained 0.55%, while Japan’s Nikkei rose 0.9%. South Korea’s KOSPI outperformed, climbing 2%.

The gains followed a stronger session on Wall Street, where technology stocks led a rebound after recent losses. Investors also took some comfort from a stabilisation in bond markets after the 10-year US Treasury yield climbed above 5% earlier this week, its highest level since 2007. The yield was last at 4.936%.

Oil prices provided another boost to sentiment, with Brent crude falling 1% to US$103.77 a barrel as traders assessed alternative routes for Middle East oil supplies. Prices remained above US$100, however, amid continued concerns over the conflict involving Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

The recent rise in oil prices has kept inflation and interest rates firmly in focus across global markets. The Federal Reserve raised rates on Wednesday for the first time in three years and signalled further increases could follow, while the Bank of England warned it may need to raise rates if the Middle East conflict continues to push up inflation.

“If bonds reverse and yields push higher again, volatility could quickly return,” said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone.

“For now, though, the buyers have regained some control, and the price action suggests the post-Fed risk-off move has lost momentum.”

BOJ Decision In Focus

The yen weakened to 156.23 per US dollar as investors awaited the BOJ’s policy decision later on Friday. The central bank is widely expected to raise its policy rate to a 31-year high.

The yen has strengthened sharply this month on expectations of faster BOJ tightening and signs that Japanese investors are repatriating funds. However, it has given up some gains this week following the Fed’s more hawkish stance.

“The key as such for markets is not just whether BOJ hikes, but also how it hikes and the communication by Governor Ueda on the path moving forward,” said Michael Wan, currency strategist at MUFG.

“With a 25 basis point hike fully priced, the hike alone should do little to support the yen,” said Sarah Hammoud, currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia.

“Governor Ueda will need to convince markets that the BOJ is inclined to hike rates at a faster pace. We expect the BOJ to hike rates again in December. We consider the risk is that Ueda fails to match the market’s hawkish expectations.”

The euro was steady at US$1.148 but was on course for a 1% weekly decline, its biggest drop since June.

Spot gold rose 0.5% to US$4,361 an ounce.

Reuters

data.title: Yen Slips With BOJ Rate Hike In Focus
data.description:
The yen weakened against the US dollar and euro on Friday as traders awaited an expected Bank of Japan (BOJ) rate hike, with the central bank’s guidance on future tightening likely to determine the currency’s next move.

The yen fell 0.1% to 156.19 per US dollar after snapping a three-day losing streak on Thursday. It was also 0.2% weaker against the euro at 179.30 yen.

Markets are pricing in an 83% chance of a BOJ rate hike, with expectations for further quarterly increases, according to LSEG data.

The BOJ is widely expected to raise its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25%, its highest level in more than three decades.

“Given the degree of pricing, the rate decision itself may have limited impact on the yen,” said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone Group in Melbourne.

“Instead, attention should fall on the forward swaps curve and the bank’s guidance around the pace and urgency of further tightening.”

“Governor Ueda’s press conference will therefore be key. The market will be looking for confirmation that further normalisation remains firmly on the table, while assessing whether the Bank sees any urgency to move again.”

The yen’s weakness came after Japanese inflation data released on Friday showed core consumer prices rose less than expected in August, potentially reducing some pressure for faster policy tightening.

Meanwhile, the US dollar index was flat at 100.21 after retreating from a 2-1/2-month high reached on Thursday.

Markets have also started pricing in a higher chance of another US Federal Reserve rate hike at its next meeting. Fed funds futures indicate a 53% probability of a 25-basis-point increase next month, up from 27.2% a week earlier, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool.

Elsewhere, sterling was flat at US$1.3359, close to a 2-1/2-month low, after the Bank of England kept interest rates unchanged and unexpectedly paused sales of government bonds for six months.

The euro was little changed at US$1.1478, while the Australian dollar gained 0.1% to US$0.7117. The New Zealand dollar slipped 0.1% to US$0.5724.

Oil prices also remained under pressure, with Brent crude falling 1% to US$103.76 a barrel as traders reassessed supply risks following fresh strikes between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

Bitcoin fell 0.1% to US$76,442.97 while ether declined 0.2% to US$2,447.39.

data.title: Bursa Finds Early Support From Wall Street Rebound
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia edged higher in early trade on Friday, with technology and semiconductor counters among the top gainers after Wall Street rebounded overnight.

The FBM KLCI rose 0.34 points or 0.02% to 1,675.08 as of early trade after opening 1.98 points higher at 1,676.72.

The overnight rebound on Wall Street was led by technology stocks, with the Nasdaq Composite climbing 1.69% to 26,418.30. The S&P 500 gained 1.14% to 7,637.74 while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.62% to 51,779.85.

Lower oil prices, easing US Treasury yields and stronger-than-expected jobs data helped investors look beyond concerns over the Federal Reserve’s first interest rate hike in more than three years.

On Bursa, Malaysian Pacific Industries surged RM1.44 to RM41.54, while Pentamaster gained 10 sen to RM5.32 and Dufu Industries rose 10 sen to RM2.74.

MI Technovation added eight sen to RM5.67, UWC gained eight sen to RM6.36 and Unisem climbed six sen to RM4.21.

Other notable gainers included Sunway Construction, which rose 16 sen to RM7.28, Paragon Union, up 10 sen to RM1.52, and Telekom Malaysia, which added six sen to RM7.86.

Meanwhile, PETRONAS Dagangan fell 34 sen to RM20.74, Nestle Malaysia declined 22 sen to RM90.30, Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia lost 12 sen to RM12.62 and Hong Leong Bank slipped 10 sen to RM23.

Berjaya Research maintained a cautious outlook on the FBM KLCI, citing elevated US Treasury yields and continued uncertainty over the global interest rate outlook.

The research house said the recent weakness could nevertheless encourage bargain hunting among fundamentally sound counters as the benchmark index approaches oversold territory.

“Investors will also be monitoring the upcoming Bank of Japan interest rate decision and Malaysia’s inflation data for further clues on the regional monetary policy outlook and domestic price pressures,” Berjaya Research said.

Technically, the research house said the index remained in a pullback phase after forming another bearish candlestick. It placed immediate resistance at 1,687 points followed by 1,700, while support was seen at 1,666 and 1,655.

Rakuten Trade meanwhile expects the market to continue consolidating, although lower oil prices and bond yields could encourage selective bargain hunting.

data.title: Ringgit Gains As West Asia Oil Fears Cool
data.description:
The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Friday as easing concerns over crude oil supplies from West Asia improved risk appetite.

At 8am, the local currency strengthened to 4.0955/1015 against the greenback from Thursday’s close of 4.0965/1010.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said sentiment improved after Saudi Arabia reportedly began restoring its damaged East-West oil pipeline, while tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz continued.

“As a result, Brent crude oil prices fell 0.95 per cent to US$104.82 per barrel, while US Treasury yields declined, with the two- and 10-year notes falling seven basis points each to 4.67 per cent and 4.94 per cent, respectively.

“However, attention has now shifted to the Bank of Japan’s (BOJ) monetary policy decision later today, with consensus expecting a 25-basis-point increase in its policy rate to 1.25 per cent,” he told Bernama.

Mohd Afzanizam said the market would be watching the BOJ’s economic assessment and policy tone closely, as a more hawkish stance could trigger further unwinding of yen carry trades and increase volatility in the foreign exchange market.

He expects the ringgit to remain in a narrow range today as traders assess the BOJ decision.

Against major currencies, the ringgit strengthened against the euro to 4.7000/7069 from 4.7003/7055 previously. It also gained against the yen to 2.6228/6268 from 2.6305/6336 and rose against the British pound to 5.4704/4784 from 5.4877/4937.

The local currency was mixed against its ASEAN peers.

It strengthened against the Singapore dollar to 3.2096/2146 from 3.2099/2137 but weakened against the Thai baht to 12.3043/3279 from 12.2734/2917.

The ringgit was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.53/6.54 and the Indonesian rupiah at 230.7/231.1.

data.title: Singapore Stocks Open Lower, STI Gives Back More Ground
data.description:
Singapore stocks opened lower on Friday, with the Straits Times Index (STI) falling 33.05 points or 0.58% to 5,627.47 as of 9:13am.

Market breadth was slightly negative, with 101 gainers against 118 decliners. Total trading volume stood at 96.68 million shares, while traded value reached S$187.90 million.

Banking counters came under pressure, with DBS falling 0.72% to S$76.39 and UOB declining to S$41.41. OCBC Bank traded at S$31.05.

Among other major counters, ST Engineering stood at S$10.55, Yangzijiang Shipbuilding traded at S$5.18, AEM was at S$9.15 and City Developments stood at S$8.21.

REITs also opened lower, with CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust falling 0.88% to S$2.26. CapitaLand Ascendas REIT traded at S$2.32, Keppel DC REIT at S$2.12 and Mapletree Logistics Trust at S$1.10.

The weaker opening came as investors continued to assess the outlook for interest rates following the US Federal Reserve’s latest rate hike and signals that further tightening could follow.

The Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday, its first increase in more than three years.

data.title: Kospi Jumps 2.5% At Open Despite Fed Rate Hike
data.description:
South Korea’s Kospi opened 2.54% higher on Friday, rebounding strongly after the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates and signalled further tightening.

The benchmark Kospi gained 170.29 points to 6,885.70 at the open, according to the Seoul Economic Daily.

The rally came despite Wall Street closing lower on Thursday following the Fed’s 25-basis-point rate increase to 3.75% to 4.00%, its first hike in more than three years.

The Fed also signalled that another rate increase could follow before the end of 2026 as inflation remains elevated.

Korean technology stocks helped drive the rebound, with investors looking beyond the higher US borrowing costs after the previous session’s selloff.

The Kosdaq also opened higher, gaining 0.97% to 830.18, while the South Korean won weakened 0.15% against the US dollar to 1,381.96.

The Kospi had closed at 6,717.97 on Thursday after foreign investors recorded about 12 trillion won in net selling.

Seoul Economic Daily

data.title: RHB Initiates Short On HSIF After Bearish Breakout
data.description:
RHB Research has shifted to a negative trading bias on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) after the index breached its 24,600-point support, with the research house initiating a short position at 24,572 points.

The HSIF opened at 24,688 points and climbed to an intraday high of 24,718 points before falling to a low of 24,330 points and closing at 24,572 points. It later recovered 95 points in evening trading to last trade at 24,667 points.

RHB Research said the bearish breakout, combined with the Relative Strength Index (RSI) turning lower, indicated that downward momentum was taking hold.

The index also closed below both moving average lines, which the research house said could attract further selling pressure and lead to a correction towards the 24,000-point level.

RHB Research closed out its previous long position initiated at 24,657 points after the 24,600-point support was breached.

The research house initiated a short position at 24,572 points based on the Sept 17 close, with a stop-loss level at 25,500 points.

The immediate support levels are at 24,000 points and 23,600 points, while resistance is seen at 25,000 points followed by 25,500 points.

data.title: Wall Street Jumps After Fed Hike As Tech Stocks Lead Recovery
data.description:
Wall Street rebounded on Thursday, led by technology stocks, as easing oil prices, lower US Treasury yields and stronger labour market data helped investors look beyond the Federal Reserve’s first interest rate hike in more than three years.

The Nasdaq Composite rose 1.69% to 26,418.30, while the S&P 500 gained 1.14% to 7,637.74. The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 0.62% to 51,779.85.

Technology stocks led gains across the S&P 500, while chip stocks and gold and silver miners each rose more than 3%. Interest rate-sensitive banks also stabilised after falling 2.3% in the previous session, with the sector index gaining 0.2%.

Oil prices fell to a one-week low after reports that Saudi Arabia was moving additional crude through Oman eased concerns over supply disruptions. However, the wider Middle East conflict continued to keep energy supply risks in focus.

The retreat in oil prices also helped ease concerns over inflation, while the 10-year US Treasury yield declined after climbing above 5% earlier in the week.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday, its first increase since July 2023, and signalled that further tightening could follow this year. Markets are now pricing in a 53.1% chance of another 25-basis-point hike at the October meeting, up from 27.2% a week earlier.

“We’re seeing interest in the areas of the market that have been hit hard in anticipation of this Fed rate hike,” said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth.

“And people sort of stepping in, doing a little bit of buying on the pullback.”

US labour market data also provided support, with initial jobless claims falling to near their lowest levels since 1969, reinforcing expectations that the economy remains resilient.

Meanwhile, crypto-linked stocks rallied after the US Securities and Exchange Commission announced a five-year exemption for tokenised stock trading. Circle Internet Group and Robinhood gained 5.8% and 5.2% respectively, while Coinbase rose 5.8%.

Among individual decliners, CoreWeave fell 4.2% after announcing plans to raise capital through stock and convertible bond offerings, while Fluence Energy tumbled 15.4% after cutting its fiscal 2026 revenue forecast.

data.title: Stock Picks: Solarvest And MN Holdings
data.description:
RHB Research has identified Solarvest Holdings Bhd and MN Holdings Bhd as stocks to watch, citing bullish technical setups and the potential for further gains if key resistance levels are breached.

Solarvest could extend its upward momentum after breaking above resistance with a bullish candlestick. RHB Research said the stock could move towards RM3.45, followed by RM3.65, if it remains above the RM3.25 breakout level.

However, a fall below the RM3.05 support level would invalidate the bullish setup and potentially trigger a correction.

Meanwhile, MN Holdings is testing its immediate resistance with a bullish candlestick, while its upward-sloping 21-day simple moving average and rising trading volume point to strengthening momentum.

RHB Research said a breakout above RM3.75 could signal a resumption of the stock’s uptrend, with the next resistance levels at RM4 and RM4.25.

A decline below the RM3.50 support level, however, could weaken market sentiment and open the way for a correction.

data.title: Stocks On Nasdaq, S&P 500 Rebound As Oil Edges Lower, Market Absorb Fed Move
data.description:
US stocks rose in premarket trading on Thursday as oil prices edged lower and an expected Fed rate hike on Wednesday offered some relief that the central bank was working to contain inflation.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.7%, while the S&P 500 climbed 1%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.4%, rebounding from a post-Fed-hike slump on Wednesday.

Stocks recovered as investors assessed Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s hawkish rhetoric, which analysts said helped restore the Fed’s credibility on inflation. On Wednesday, the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points for the first time in three years and projected one more rate hike this year.

data.title: Pioneer Heat Closes ACE Market Debut 20% Above IPO Price
data.description:
Pioneer Heat Holdings Bhd ended its maiden trading day on the ACE Market at 30 sen, a 20% premium to its 25 sen IPO price, after drawing strong investor interest throughout the session.

The mechanical and civil engineering services provider opened at 25.5 sen before climbing to 27.5 sen by 9.01am on 10.44 million shares. The counter strengthened further to 32.5 sen at midday, with 66.82 million shares traded, before settling at 30 sen at the close on turnover of 80.18 million shares.

The debut followed strong demand for Pioneer Heat’s IPO, which was oversubscribed by 47.8 times after receiving 9,512 applications for 846.47 million shares.

Pioneer Heat raised RM21.68 million in gross proceeds from the issuance of 86.7 million new shares.

Of the proceeds, RM7.9 million will go towards working capital, RM4.01 million for machinery and equipment, RM4 million for a new Sendayan headquarters and RM2.07 million for a new Sarawak office. Another RM3.7 million has been set aside for listing expenses.

Speaking to BusinessToday ahead of the listing, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director Wong Wei Ken said the group was ready to move into its next phase of growth after building its technical capabilities and track record over 29 years.

“Having built our technical capabilities and track record over 29 years, we believe the group has reached a stage where we are ready to scale the business further,” he said.

Working capital represents 36.4% of the IPO proceeds and will support subcontractor services, materials, tools, consumables and performance bonds.

Wong said the added liquidity would allow the group to bid for more tenders and undertake a larger number of projects simultaneously.

“As our business grows, larger projects and a higher number of projects being executed concurrently will naturally require more working capital,” he said.

Pioneer Heat is also looking to deepen its presence in Sarawak, where its subsidiaries have secured Petroleum Sarawak Bhd vendor registration, opening the door to quotation and tender opportunities in the state’s oil and gas sector.

Wong said Sarawak’s oil and gas and petrochemical industries were closely aligned with Pioneer Heat’s capabilities in piping system engineering, heat treatment, flange management and non-destructive testing.

“We are seeing opportunities in Sarawak’s oil and gas and petrochemical industries, which align closely with the group’s capabilities,” he said.

As at July 22, Pioneer Heat had an unbilled order book of RM50.43 million, comprising RM38.15 million from mechanical engineering services and RM12.28 million from civil engineering projects.

For the first quarter ended June 30, 2026, the group recorded revenue of RM29.65 million and profit after tax of RM2.83 million.

Wong said Pioneer Heat’s longer-term ambition is to broaden its domestic footprint and take on larger, more technically complex projects.

“Ultimately, we want Pioneer Heat to be recognised as a trusted and established mechanical engineering services provider,” he said.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Ends Lower As US Yield, Fed Concerns Weigh
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia closed lower on Sept 17 after a volatile session, with the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) losing 4.47 points as rising US Treasury yields and concerns over further monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve weighed on investor sentiment.

At 5pm, the FBM KLCI settled at 1,674.74, down from the close of 1,679.21 on Sept 15. The benchmark moved between an intraday low of 1,670.75 and a high of 1,684.92.

The local bourse resumed trading after being closed on Sept 16 in conjunction with the Malaysia Day public holiday.

The broader market also finished mostly weaker. The FBM 70 slipped 8.42 points to 17,607.23, while the FBM Emas fell 29.11 points to 12,414.82. The FBM Shariah declined 28.55 points to 12,273.87, while the F4GBM shed 2.36 points to 1,006.95.

Trading activity picked up, with total turnover rising to 3.6 billion units worth RM3.25 billion from 3.34 billion units valued at RM3.25 billion on Sept 15.

Zetrix AI Bhd was the most actively traded counter, slipping one sen to 24.5 sen on 293.62 million shares.

AirAsia Group Bhd followed, falling 13.5 sen to 50.5 sen on 155.58 million shares, while Capital A Bhd lost 4.5 sen to 23 sen on 135 million shares.

New ACE Market debutant Pioneer Heat Holdings Bhd bucked the weaker market, finishing at 30 sen, five sen or 20% above its 25 sen IPO price, on 80.18 million shares.

TWL Holdings Bhd was unchanged at 2.5 sen on 66 million shares.

The softer close came as investors remained cautious over elevated US bond yields and the prospect that the Federal Reserve could maintain a tighter monetary policy stance, keeping pressure on risk appetite across regional markets.

data.title: Hong Leong Bank, PetChem Lead Bursa Losers As ViTrox Tops Gainers
data.description:
Hong Leong Bank Bhd and Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd (PetChem) led Bursa Malaysia’s biggest decliners, while ViTrox Corp Bhd emerged as the top gainer as market breadth remained subdued.

Hong Leong Bank shed 36 sen, or 1.5%, to close at RM23.10, making it the day’s biggest loser by absolute price movement. PetChem followed closely, sliding 34 sen, or 6.5%, to RM4.86 on 14.15 million shares.

Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd declined 26 sen to RM22.86, while Hong Leong Financial Group Bhd dropped 22 sen to RM18.56.

Bursa Malaysia Bhd rounded out the five biggest losers, falling 18 sen to RM8.07.

Selling pressure outweighed buying interest across the broader market, with 673 decliners against 465 gainers. Another 548 counters were unchanged, 1,170 untraded and 13 suspended.

On the upside, automated test equipment maker ViTrox led gainers with a 48-sen, or 5.3%, jump to RM9.58 on 4.65 million shares.

Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd advanced 40 sen to RM40.10, while Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd climbed 36 sen to RM12.74.

Nestlé (M) Bhd gained 34 sen to RM90.52, while Petronas Dagangan Bhd added 30 sen to RM21.08.

Trading activity strengthened, with market turnover rising to 3.6 billion units worth RM3.25 billion compared to 3.34 billion units valued at RM3.25 billion on Sept 15.
